4.translation: BED starts at zero and excludes the right endpoint. Read the pUC19 origin interval and compare the coordinates before and after import.

7.translation: PAF gives the full sequence lengths and alignment spans. Select alignments with mapq ≥ 30, then collect both sequences and their lengths for plotting.

12.translation: A reverse alignment has descending subject coordinates. Use the converted coordinates directly for plotting.

14.translation: Convert one interval and then an interval pair. Full lengths come from `seqlengths`. Install GenomicRanges for the first example and InteractionSet for the second.

20.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ reads six required tab-separated fields, optional name/score/two strands and additional metadata. The first anchor stays query and the second stays subject. Scores remain strings; neither Identity nor read support is inferred. The format follows the [BEDPE description](⟦shared:1⟧).

21.translation: This example re-encodes the intervals of bundled observed alignments for a coordinate round trip; it is not paired-read evidence. Six columns contain no strand evidence, so the imported anchor strands and relative direction remain unknown. Supply real strand columns when known; do not infer them from ascending coordinates.

23.translation: Negative-strand anchors use decreasing canonical endpoints, consistent with paired-interval adapters; the original start/end and strand fields are also retained. Names are not assumed unique. Extra columns remain in ⟦shared:0⟧, named ⟦shared:1⟧ onwards. Unknown chromosomes (⟦shared:2⟧) and boundaries (⟦shared:3⟧) fail by default. Explicit ⟦shared:4⟧ retains incomplete rows for auditing; filter ⟦shared:5⟧ before adaptation or plotting. Invalid known coordinates and zero-width intervals always fail. For interval ribbons without Identity, set a constant fill explicitly rather than manufacturing pident.
